start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:get-found-in-search-and-answer-engines for https://bakery.example.com, questions: who makes the best sourdough in town and where can I pre-order a wedding cake, engines: ChatGPT and Perplexity."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it writes one search-visibility record to your own records so the next run can compare, and its answers sit on the run record.
instructions: 1. Give your site, the reader questions to ask and the engines; check_rows is optional.
2. Say "Run workflow:get-found-in-search-and-answer-engines". It lists every page from the sitemap, then scores each page the way an engine reads it.
3. Read the proposed /robots.txt, /llms.txt and per-page changes; facts it does not have are listed as needing you.
4. It publishes only through a destination tool you have connected that can save a draft, preview, publish and read back; otherwise it reports the exact missing operation and stops.
5. Read the before-and-after scores and which engines name or cite your site for which question.

worked_examples.title: List the pages of a bakery site
worked_examples.ask: Get my bakery site found by answer engines.

questions: Who makes the best sourdough in town?
Where can I pre-order a wedding cake?

worked_examples.given: Read from the row of workflow:get-found-in-search-and-answer-engines in tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json: step list-pages reads <origin>/sitemap.xml with tool:read-public-web-page and answers {sitemap, pages}. The sitemap lists the home page, /menu and /wedding-cakes.
